decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Save a bookmark (P1) — enter an address + optional title, it's stored and listed'. Round 1 client: 'Approved... save... features are sufficient'.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saving by URL conforms to reference; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Browse & open bookmarks (P1) — see the list, click to open in a new tab'. Round 3 maker: 'List newest-first, open in a new tab'. Client approved (round 1/3).
decisions.note: Specification/implementation review. List display + open-original conform to reference. Favicon absence is captured under the auto-metadata divergence, not double-counted here.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Edit & delete (P2) — fix titles/addresses, remove with confirmation'. Round 1 client approved edit/delete as sufficient.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Edit and delete conform to reference; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Organize & find (P3) — tags, tag filtering, and text search'. Round 3 maker: 'Tag filter + live text search (combined with AND)'. Client approved tag/search as sufficient.
decisions.note: Specification/implementation review. Tag assignment, tag filtering, and full-text search conform to reference core items; recorded conforming decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker 'Key assumptions' table: 'Page metadata | No auto-fetching titles/favicons/previews'. Round 1 client: 'Approved. Those v1 assumptions are acceptable...'. Reaffirmed round 2 maker ('No... auto-fetched page titles/favicons — as approved').
decisions.note: Specification gate. Divergence from REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/description/favicon/preview) and REF-BM-03 (edit auto-collected metadata) established independently. Client gives blanket 'assumptions are acceptable' — does not identify the specific expectation or difference, so it is bare approval, not accepted_divergence. Counted once (round 2 is reaffirmation, not a new decision).

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker 'Key assumptions' table: 'Import/export | Not included (no browser-bookmark import)'. Round 1 client: 'Approved. Those v1 assumptions are acceptable'.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Divergence from REF-BM-30 (Netscape HTML import) and REF-BM-31 (export) established. Client blanket approval does not name this exclusion or express an expectation about it; not accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: 'duplicates warn but don't block'. Round 3 client: 'The implemented app covers the behavior I approved... I accept this first version.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. REF-BM-06 requires re-saving an existing url to guide the user to edit the existing bookmark instead of creating a new one (preventing duplicates); 'warn but don't block' still permits duplicate creation, so it diverges. Client accepts the app generally without identifying this behavior or expressing the expected convergence-to-edit; unexpressed.
